OTTO - THE LOAN SHARK

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Meet a man who makes a living out of ripping off people desperate for finance – Otto van Tonder is not the finance guru you were hoping for – instead he’s just another low life conman.

Unique Selling Point:
GOOD CONSUMER EDUCATION OPPORTUNITY IN TERMS OF GETTING FINANCE.

A CROOK THAT PRESENTS HIMSELF AS A FINANCE GURU WILL GET SCHOOLED ABOUT THE LAW WHEN WE EXPOSE HIS DODGY DEALS.

OTTO IS SO RIDICULOUS – HE’s FUNNY AND DISGUSTING AT THE SAME TIME…. EEEEIIIIUUUUWWW!

Summary:
What’s worse than a bad credit record when you desperately need to secure finance? Getting ripped off by the people who promise to help you.

Otto van Tonder runs a business where he promises to organize finance through a network of so-called investors – no need for credit checks, it’s all legit he says – there’s a loop hole in the National Credit Act he says….

Once he has you conned, sorry I mean convinced, a deposit and admin fee is due – once it’s paid, there’s suddenly an issue with investors and the finance doesn’t arrive.


Further information:
THE CON
Otto van Tonder runs a business - RENT 2 KEEP CARS. He will organize you finance through a network of investors for a car. He claims to register a company, the car will be bought through the company and then leased to you on a monthly basis.

While he sells the idea as peer to peer lending – he says it’s foolproof because technically it’s a business renting you the car, not a person. THIS IS ALL NONSENSE! I’ve already done company searches with the some of the case studies information - the companies are not registered in the case studies names. Otto just makes up random company names that aren’t registered and in any case the money doesn’t seem to materialize.

I have a list of 19 victims that have paid Otto anything between R4000 and R20 000 for finance that never happened. I also have access to ex-employees that will spill the beans.

Otto does most of the deals via the net – lists his physical home address as the business address – but no one ever goes there because this victims are usually from Gauteng and don’t have the means to travel to him – that’s why they need the finance.

I know it sounds like insignificant amounts – but these people have contacted us with the story – they are our viewers too.

NOT OTTO’s FIRST RODEO
Otto previously ran a similar operation offering finance for property – here he was taking bigger deposits from clients and not delivering either resulting in them losing the properties they were hoping to buy. Chad Thomas from IRS Investigations has the background to these deals.

UNDERCOVER FOOTAGE
I’ve met with Otto – he explains the grand plan to me and promises it’s all legit. I asked about properties and he said that’s more difficult to arrange the big finance – said it’s easier to do smaller amounts for cars. He also tells me about his big plans to start an app where he’ll pair up investors with people looking for loans – MONEY FOR THE PEOPLE, BY THE PEOPLE! Accept this already exisits… All he is doing is taking money from the people that can least afford to lose the cash.






Extra Budget Items:
Might need extra half day with presenter for travel to Rustenburg for the confront

Press Release:


Otto van Tonder
What’s worse than a bad credit record when you desperately need to secure finance? Getting ripped off by the people who promise to help you. Otto van Tonder presents himself as a financial guru who’s got solutions to all your bad debt, but he’s actually a cunning conman offering affordable vehicle finance. Carte Blanche exposes a scamster preying on desperate consumers.


Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: In South Africa more people have debt than jobs – South African citizens are amongst the biggest borrowers in the world according to the World Bank.

LINK: Finance is something that everyone needs at as some stage in their lives – but with over 9.8 million South Africans with bad credit records – your options for getting finance can be limited – but if you do a simple search online – there are endless sites offering you a way out.

VO: Otto van Tonder from Rustenburg is one of these so-called financial guru’s, claiming to save the day for cash strapped South Africans.

So this is how it works: Otto will finance a car through his network of investors. He registers a company with the prospective client and himself as directors, the car is bought through the company and then leased to the client on a monthly basis.

CHAD: // I can tell you people are not getting what he’s promising them INT1 M6

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: Something about no credit checks…. // no bank statements…I don’t’ care a fuck//

VO: Private investigator Chad Thomas is all too familiar with these types of schemes that often leave consumers out of pocket – he says Otto van Tonder’s is no different.

CHAD: it looks extremely legitimate – not only is he asking you for a small admin fee, he asking for first months instalment on the vehicle, he’s asking you pay towards tracker and insurance – it all seems extremely professional // CUT END INT3 M1 //

VO: Single mum of four, Rose Onwuasor thought this was the solution she had been waiting for.

ROSE: // I was really excited I’ve been trying for so many years to get a car and it sounds awesome.// me not having a car meant me not having a job. //

VO: Rose had to pay R4850 up front for her deal with Otto’s company – Car Loans Warehouse – but before signing up, Rose did some checks online.

ROSE: I typed in the company name he was dealing under // it’s a company in the UK // and that logo matched when he sent me the paperwork it matched the logo on google – so it thought it was legit// INT1 M8

VO: Otto insists it’s legit and that the National Credit Act doesn’t apply, because according to him, it’s NOT a credit agreement – it’s a rental agreement.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: NOT THE CREDIT …. I don’t have to do an affordability test.

VO: Well it’s not quite accurate for a number a reasons – while Otto may choose not to call this arrangement a credit agreement – it simulates a credit transaction according the National Creditor Regulator’s Investigation & Enforcement Manager, Jacqueline Peters.

JACQUELINE: A very loose definition of what is credit in terms of this act is where there have been exchange, goods, service or money between two parties, there has been deferment of payment, there is an interest, charge or fee. INT1 M7

VO: But besides the National Credit Act’s rules & regulations – the fact is – Rose never got her car, nor did our other 13 case studies that signed up with Otto.

OTHER CASE STUDIES – UPSOUNDS
TIAAN STUWIG: I paid him R4850 & never got anything
MELANIE FRANK: I paid him R1183 8 & he never ever received my car

VO: We decided to pay Otto a visit at his head quarters being run from his home in Rustenburg.

DEVI: I have people who have people who paid you deposit and didn’t get the cars… lists names….
OTTO: I know there is people that I owe money but I am refunding them their deposit…INT1 M17

VO: Rose has been waiting since October last year. She accompanied us to meet Otto.

Devi: Do you know what that 5000 meant to her – tell him
ROSE: I have kids? Do you ever think they have problems - I wanted you to see my face…
OTTO: Sorry – in situation – hopefully be in situation to pay back – not intention to not refund you INT1 M44

VO: Confused about Otto’s connection to the UK based Car Loan Warehouse, we asked him for clarity.

DEVI: Is it affiliated to the UK
OTTO: No… //
DEVI: are you sure? Explain this to me?
OTTO: no law that says I can’t do it? INT1 M37
DEVI: took someone else logo
OTTO happens all the time
DEVI theft!
OTTO: no trademark on the logo in SA…. INT1 M39
DEVI: impression
OTTO: // I made mistake using logo – will own up to the fact – I never ever created that people can think that – never my intention INT1 M38

VO: Otto believes his intentions are much more honourable.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: money for the people form the people….

VO: But that’s all pie in the sky… this isn’t Otto’s first failed financing venture according to Chad.

CHAD: he was previously involved in a business called bond-a-property – very similar modus operandi – you would pay money up front so that they could arrange peer to peer funding so you could get the house of your dreams // INT3 M5

LINK: People with bad credit ratings aren’t the only ones who look for alternate financing – self-employed individuals also struggle because they don’t earn a regular income - you may think it’s a lifeline – but it could cost you everything //

JACKIE: We tried all over – because you work for yourself it’s a lot of paperwork – declined, declined – Otto came back – he can help me… INT1 M4

VO: In 2014, self-employed Jackie Pryce, applied to Otto’s property finance business to buy the house they’d been renting. He paid an amount of R12 500 to get the paperwork started.

But like with the car schemes, the finance didn’t materialise//

DEVI: How long did it take you to realise there was a problem?
JACKIE: As soon as the owner’s lawyers got involved, he then got quiet, I asked if I can get my money back, // so he did agree to give it back to me INT2 M4

DEVI: Where is Jackie Pryce’s money?
OTTO: Well, unfortunately that went into my business…
DEVI: Sorry for Jackie Pryce?
OTTO: yah, I am sorry for him… INT1 M34
DEVI: // Nowhere here does it say you may loose your money because I may not find an investor… that is wrong!
OTTO: // That is your opinion – that has to be in the contract

LINK: Otto uses legitimate concepts to reel unsuspecting clients – throwing in terms like crowd funding, peer to peer lending – and insisting his scheme is exempt from the national credit act - making the deal look authentic and almost innovative - but it’s not completely true.

JACQUELINE: // This agreement as I can see has been created almost to navigate from complying with these rules – so one you’re saying I’m going to enter to this elaborate scheme to avoid doing an affordability assessment on you or trying to comply with various provisions of the act disclosing the interest the fees and the costs. INT1 M10

VO: Let’s look at the breakdown of Rose’s deal – she was buying a car valued at R100 000. But just the rental fee of R3800 over 60 months will bring the total to a steep R228 000.

Her monthly instalment would also include a R500 ‘admin fee’ – Otto is adamant there’s no interest and therefor falls outside of the National Credit Act.

JACQUELINE: Many people fall flat when they think that it’s only interest, so if you are adding a fee or a charge then it becomes a credit agreement and that is what makes you a credit provider under the act. INT1 M7

DEVI: How do you make your money?
OTTO: I make my money by adding on 10% to the rental INT1 M11//I can charge an admin fee because not one of these transactions falls under the national credit act because they are between juristic persons. INT1M12

LINK: Some juristic persons are excluded – but not ALL - if the company has an asset value or annual turnover of less than R1m it falls under the National Credit Act and Otto and his companies fall into the category – he’s not exempt.

VO: Something he refused to concede - insisting he has studied the act.

DEVI: Are you a regulated credit provider? NO!
OTTO: Because I don’t have to be under the credit…. INT1 M28
DEVI: What you’ve done is you’ve used other people’s money to bankroll your idea and you haven’t paid them back – that’s what happened. INT1 M50

DEVI: He cant argue himself out of this?
JACQUELINE: The law is quite clear. INT3 M1 // at the end of the day the courts are going to look what was the true intention between the parties – so you can create these elaborate schemes but the courts can actually see through it. // INT1 M15

VO: Chad says Otto is the focus of multiple police investigations and his days are numbered.

DEVI: What is Otto guilty of?
CHAD: It’s theft under false pretences
DEVI: As simple as that?
CHAD: As simple as that. INT3 M13

VO: Otto is reluctant to admit his scheme is a failure and constantly blames illusive investors.

DEVI: Why did you enter into those agreements with these people then?
OTTO: no, I had prospective lenders – we are talking – what was first the chicken or the eggs….
DEVI: I’ll tell you what comes first – you find the funding before you offer somebody the service.// It’s not a chicken and egg situation //INT1 M24

VO: The only people feeling the punch, are the ones that signed up for a financing lifeline with Otto. While the losses may seem small, Chad says the volume of deals, all add up.

CHAD: he’s not a small time crook – // he is a white collar criminal. INT3 M19 - // A bottom feeder – someone who preys on the vulnerable, someone one that looks for victims themselves don’t qualify for traditional finance // // he’s an absolute rubbish. INT3 M10



PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: We expose a man offering finance solutions to people desperate for credit. But he’s no finance guru – the deals are dodgy and the clients get ripped off.

PROMO 2
VO: What’s worse than a bad credit record when you desperately need to secure finance? Getting ripped off by man that promises to help you.

CHAD: he’s not a small time crook – // he is a white collar criminal.

VO: We expose a so-called finance guru.


PROMO 3
VO: A finance guru promises unsuspecting clients a credit solution that is supposedly except from the law.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: Something about no credit checks…. // no bank statements…I

VO: We investigate this elaborate scheme.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Meet a man who makes a living out of ripping off people desperate for finance – Otto van Tonder is not the finance guru you were hoping for – instead he’s just another low life conman.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: GOOD CONSUMER EDUCATION OPPORTUNITY IN TERMS OF GETTING FINANCE. A CROOK THAT PRESENTS HIMSELF AS A FINANCE GURU WILL GET SCHOOLED ABOUT THE LAW WHEN WE EXPOSE HIS DODGY DEALS. OTTO IS SO RIDICULOUS – HE’s FUNNY AND DISGUSTING AT THE SAME TIME…. EEEEIIIIUUUUWWW!
metadata.Summary: What’s worse than a bad credit record when you desperately need to secure finance? Getting ripped off by the people who promise to help you. Otto van Tonder runs a business where he promises to organize finance through a network of so-called investors – no need for credit checks, it’s all legit he says – there’s a loop hole in the National Credit Act he says…. Once he has you conned, sorry I mean convinced, a deposit and admin fee is due – once it’s paid, there’s suddenly an issue with investors and the finance doesn’t arrive.
metadata.Further information: THE CON Otto van Tonder runs a business - RENT 2 KEEP CARS. He will organize you finance through a network of investors for a car. He claims to register a company, the car will be bought through the company and then leased to you on a monthly basis. While he sells the idea as peer to peer lending – he says it’s foolproof because technically it’s a business renting you the car, not a person. THIS IS ALL NONSENSE! I’ve already done company searches with the some of the case studies information - the companies are not registered in the case studies names. Otto just makes up random company names that aren’t registered and in any case the money doesn’t seem to materialize. I have a list of 19 victims that have paid Otto anything between R4000 and R20 000 for finance that never happened. I also have access to ex-employees that will spill the beans. Otto does most of the deals via the net – lists his physical home address as the business address – but no one ever goes there because this victims are usually from Gauteng and don’t have the means to travel to him – that’s why they need the finance. I know it sounds like insignificant amounts – but these people have contacted us with the story – they are our viewers too. NOT OTTO’s FIRST RODEO Otto previously ran a similar operation offering finance for property – here he was taking bigger deposits from clients and not delivering either resulting in them losing the properties they were hoping to buy. Chad Thomas from IRS Investigations has the background to these deals. UNDERCOVER FOOTAGE I’ve met with Otto – he explains the grand plan to me and promises it’s all legit. I asked about properties and he said that’s more difficult to arrange the big finance – said it’s easier to do smaller amounts for cars. He also tells me about his big plans to start an app where he’ll pair up investors with people looking for loans – MONEY FOR THE PEOPLE, BY THE PEOPLE! Accept this already exisits… All he is doing is taking money from the people that can least afford to lose the cash.
